title: Let Us Join, as God Commands
description: Let Us Join, as God Commands in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 905 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Call to Social Worship”, where the book credits them to the Methodist Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let us join, as God com-mands, Let us join our hearts and hands, Help to gain our call-ing's hope; Help to build each oth-er up; Car-ry on the Christ-ian's strife; Walk in ho-li-ness of life; Faith-ful-ly our gifts im-prove For the sake of him we love;

lines: Let us join, as God commands,
Let us join our hearts and hands,
Help to gain our calling's hope;
Help to build each other up;
Carry on the Christian's strife;
Walk in holiness of life;
Faithfully our gifts improve
For the sake of him we love; —
Still forget the things behind;
Follow Christ in heart and mind;
Toward the mark unwearied press;
Seize the crown of righteousness,
While we walk with God in light,
God our hearts will still unite;
Dearest fellowship we prove —
Fellowship in Jesus, love.
Still, O Lord, our faith increase;
Cleanse from all unrighteousness:
Thee th' unholy cannot see:
Make, O make us meet for thee:
Every vile affection kill;
Root out every seed of ill;
Utterly abolish sin;
Write thy law of love within.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
